headline: HIV Infections Hit 30-Year Low as Treatment Breakthroughs Accelerate
meta_description: New HIV infections and AIDS deaths are at their lowest in over 30 years, with 7 countries achieving 80% infection reductions and revolutionary prevention medic…
summary_short: HIV infections and AIDS deaths have reached their lowest levels in more than 30 years, as new prevention medicines and expanded treatment access transform the global res…
body:
New HIV infections and AIDS-related deaths have fallen to their lowest levels in more than three decades, according to a landmark UNAIDS report unveiled at the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro. The findings mark a pivotal moment in the decades-long fight against the virus: seven countries—Benin, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Nepal, Rwanda, and Zimbabwe—have achieved nearly an 80% reduction in new infections since 2010. Meanwhile, 11 countries have reached the "95-95-95" treatment targets, meaning virtually all people living with HIV know their status, access antiretroviral therapy, and achieve viral suppression. These milestones underscore what was once unimaginable: that ending AIDS is genuinely within reach.

The momentum extends beyond treatment to prevention. Revolutionary new medicines are shifting the landscape—monthly and six-month injections are rolling into markets worldwide, while monthly pills remain in late-stage trials. A breakthrough trial of lenacapavir, one such prevention injection, showed zero HIV infections among 3,200 young female participants, a result that seemed impossible just years ago. Countries are mobilizing quickly: Brazil increased access to HIV prevention medicines by 41% in a single year, while South Africa negotiates pricing for twice-yearly injections, and Ethiopia and Uganda expand programs through domestic funding.

To scale these gains, UNITAID and the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria have committed resources to deliver lenacapavir to 3 million people by 2028. Despite the obstacles that remain, the convergence of scientific breakthroughs, expanded access, and renewed political will suggests the world is entering what UNAIDS calls an "HIV prevention revolution." The message from global health leaders is clear: the finish line is visible.
quick_facts: HIV infections and AIDS deaths at lowest levels in 30+ years
Seven countries achieved 80% reduction in new infections since 2010
Eleven countries met the 95-95-95 treatment targets globally
Prevention injection lenacapavir showed zero infections in 3,200 participants
Partners pledged to reach 3 million people with new medicines by 2028
